name: Apple Raita

ingredients.name: kosher salt, plus more to taste
crisp, sweet-tart apple (such as Pink Lady or Honeycrisp)

instructions.primary_message: In a large bowl, combine yogurt, salt, sugar, cumin, and chile powder, then whisk to combine. Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Just before serving, quarter and core apple. Using the large holes of a box grater, grate the flesh of each apple quarter until only the skin remains. Discard skin.
Transfer grated apple to yogurt mixture and stir well to combine. Season to taste with salt.
Top raita with cilantro, if using. Serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: apple raita, raita, indian recipes, yogurt sauce, yogurt dip

description: This easy 5-minute apple raita combines crisp, sweet-tart apple with creamy yogurt, cumin, and Kashmiri chile for a cooling, crunchy side.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Finely chopped fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems, for serving (optional)

Notes: This recipe can easily be doubled.
Kashmiri chile powder, available at Indian grocery stores and online, has moderate heat, a slightly fruity flavor, and a vibrant red color. If unavailable, substitute sweet paprika with a pinch of cayenne.
Grate the apple just before serving to minimize browning.

Make-ahead and storage: The yogurt mixture can be prepared through step 1 up to 4 days in advance and refrigerated in an airtight container.
Apple raita is best enjoyed shortly after it’s made while the apple is still crisp and vibrant, but leftovers can be safely refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Kaumudi Marathé
